subject: Re: Redwood SDK onboarding & observability checklist for Helios Health
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kelsey Turner <kelsey@helioshealth.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@helioshealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood SDK onboarding & observability checklist for Helios Health

Kelsey / Sam —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps focused on integration, auth, routing, and observability so your infra team can plan the work: 

1) SDK & auth
- Languages: you confirmed Python for server-side inference and TypeScript for the frontend edge runner.
- Auth: initial plan is API key for dev + short-lived signed tokens (KMS-backed) for prod. We recommend header X-Redwood-Role for routing (e.g., routing to low-latency vs cost-optimized model pools).

2) Structured outputs / tool calling
- We'll enable function/tool-calling for appointment-scheduling workflows. We propose a JSON schema v1 for structured output (sample in attachment).

3) Embeddings / reranker
- You want embeddings for semantic search + a small reranker model (on dedicated capacity) to improve recall precision. We'll provide the ReRanker v0.3 profile.

4) Observability hooks (critical asks from your SRE)
- Trace propagation: Redwood will echo incoming X-Request-Id and return X-Redwood-Trace: <trace_id>. Please surface this end-to-end.
- Latency breakdown headers: X-Redwood-Latency-Total, X-Redwood-Latency-Kernel, X-Redwood-Latency-KV-Cache-Hit.
- Logging fields: request_id, trace_id, model_name, quant_profile, batch_size, cache_hit (true/false).
- Metrics / dashboards: per-route token cost, 95th/99th latency, KV cache hit rate. We'll share a Grafana dashboard template.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup-guide.pdf (quickstart), integration-checklist.xlsx (tasks/owners), helios-network-map.drawio (your network notes from call).

Proposed owners / dates:
- Integration workshop (live): week of Dec 8 — Connor + Redwood infra eng
- Observability dashboard handoff & sample dashboards: Marissa to deliver by Dec 15
- Security artefacts (SOC2 evidence + KMS flow): I'll loop Laura after you confirm which artifacts are needed.

Can you confirm: SDK languages, whether your SRE can accept our X-Redwood-* headers, and availability for a 60-minute integration workshop on Dec 8 or Dec 9 (PST)?

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
Schedule: https://cal.redwood.com/connor

From: Kelsey Turner <kelsey@helioshealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@helioshealth.com>, it@helioshealth.com
Date: 2026-12-01T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK onboarding & observability checklist for Helios Health

Connor —

Thanks for the detailed recap. Confirming a few items from our side so we can line up the infra team: 

- Languages: yes, Python (backend microservices) + TypeScript (customer-facing UI).
- Auth: agree on API key for dev environments; for prod we need short-lived tokens issued via our KMS. Can you share the token exchange flow (sample code)?
- Headers: accepting X-Redwood-Trace and X-Redwood-Latency-* headers is fine. We will want these forwarded into our Splunk ingestion.
- Embeddings & reranker: we prefer embeddings stored in our Vector DB (we use Pinecone). Reranker on dedicated capacity is preferred for consistency.

Questions:
1) Can KV cache hits be exposed as a Prometheus metric (rather than only an HTTP header)? Our SRE prefers pulling metrics.
2) For function-calling, we need a versioned JSON schema and examples.

Availability: Dec 9 (10:00–11:00 PST) works best for the integration workshop.

Kelsey Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | Helios Health
kelsey@helioshealth.com

On Dec 1, 2026, at 14:05, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:

Subject: Re: Redwood SDK onboarding & observability checklist for Helios Health

Kelsey —

Great, thanks for confirming. Answers inline below and updated action items.

- Token exchange flow: attaching a short Python example and a snippet for our auth server (see redwood-sdk-setup-guide.pdf). We'll also add a TypeScript snippet before the workshop.
- Metrics: yes — we can export KV cache hits and cache_hit_rate as Prometheus metrics. We'll include metric names: redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Function-calling: will provide versioned JSON schema v1.1 and a working example that returns typed JSON with a top-level "tool_invocations" array.

Updated owners/dates: 
- Integration workshop (Dec 9, 10:00–11:00 PST) — Connor, Marissa, Redwood infra engineer (TBD) — goal: get first request through SDK and validate trace propagation.
- Prometheus metrics and Grafana template — Marissa to deliver by Dec 15.
- Token exchange example & TypeScript snippet — Connor to add to the Drive by Dec 6.
- Security docs requested (SOC2 evidence + KMS flow) — Laura will confirm scope after Kelsey lists required artefacts.

I'll open a short Jira INF-2319 to track the Prometheus/observability work and link to the Drive.

Attachments again: integration-checklist.xlsx (row-level owners and dates).

Cheers,
Connor

Hi team —

I'll own the Prometheus + Grafana deliverable and confirm metric names and a dashboard JSON by Dec 15. A couple of notes from a pricing / procurement angle: 

- For the reranker on Dedicated, we recommend a 3-month trial commitment to measure quality delta before committing to annual reserved capacity.
- If Helios wants a reduced unit price for a 6-12 month reserved commit, loop Laura for approval on the discount. Laura — can you confirm the approval threshold for discounts (percent / ARR)?

I'll upload the initial Grafana template and a sample dashboards link to the Drive tonight.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa / Connor —

Thanks — Dec 9 at 10:00 PST is confirmed for the integration workshop. Attendees: my SRE lead Sam, myself, and two infra engineers (joining via Hangouts link).

We want the following included on the call:
- Live demo: trace propagation end-to-end (X-Request-Id -> X-Redwood-Trace) and Splunk ingestion mapping.
- Prometheus metric names and exporter format for KV cache hits.
- Example flow for function-calling with our appointment API (we'll provide API schema before the call).

Procurement: Sam will start a request for a 3-month trial for the reranker; we'll convert to reserved capacity after quality checks. We'll need a simple SOW and a draft PO template — Marissa, can you share a template?

Finally: please add INF-2319 to the workshop agenda and include the Grafana template link in the calendar invite.

See you on Dec 9.

Kelsey Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | Helios Health
